Hi Alyssa — thanks, and welcome. Looping Billing (Vanessa) and FinOps (Naomi) so we can get you onto the right lane. Quick answers up front: 

- Marketplace vs Direct: For AWS Marketplace we support both marketplace-managed billing (recommended if you want consolidated AWS billing) and direct invoicing. If you pick marketplace billing, the AWS flow handles settlement and we only need the marketplace seller ID and listing metadata. For direct invoicing we require a PO (from your procurement) and Redwood will invoice directly.
- NET30: We can enable NET30 on a per-deal basis. For marketplace-listing-driven purchases we typically route through marketplace billing, but if you need NET30 on direct invoices we'll request credit approval from FinOps.
- Tax/docs: For a US entity we need a completed W-9 (EIN) + vendor intake form. For EU entities we need VAT registration evidence and the legal entity name as appears on invoices.
- Seller/listing ID: Please provide the marketplace seller ID or the desired Listing SKU so we can map billing and support routing.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Return the attached vendor_checklist_marketplace.pdf + completed intake form with legal entity, EIN, and billing contact.
2) Attach your W-9 for U.S. tax validation (or VAT docs for EU).
3) Confirm whether you want marketplace billing (AWS/GCP/Azure) or Redwood direct invoices with PO/NET30.

If you want, Vanessa can send our bank wiring/invoice header example and a sample invoice template so your AP team can test. Once we have docs we'll open an internal ticket and (if needed) submit the NET30 request to FinOps.

I'm copying Laura from Partner Ops to help with listing mapping.

Thanks — I can review the packet as soon as you send it.

— Hannah Schmitt
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
